Yes, the Illinois mail-in ballot application system includes several safeguards designed to prevent a single person from voting multiple times. According to the evidence, these safeguards include:

*   **Request Rejection:** Once an application has been processed, any subsequent requests from that same voter are rejected.
*   **Legal Deterrents:** Attempting to vote multiple times is classified as a felony.

statements.statement: The man in the claim received four ballot applications, not four actual ballots, which were sent by the Center for Voter Information (CVI) that only mails applications to registered voters; even if a person returns multiple ballot applications, they are only permitted to vote once, and Tom Lopach, CEO of CVI, stated that returning multiple applications would only increase the workload for local election officials rather than allowing multiple votes.
statements.support_span: The man did not receive four ballots; he received four ballot applications. | They were sent to him by the Center for Voter Information (CVI)... Please bear in mind that the Center for Voter Information only mails ballot applications to registered voters. CVI does not send out actual ballots. | Even if the man returned all four applications, he would only be allowed to vote once, according to state officials and the CEO and president of the nonprofit group that sent out the applications. | If the mail recipient on this Facebook post were to return all four ballot applications to his local election office, he would still only be allowed to vote once. All he would be doing is adding to the workload of local election officials.

statements.statement: Michigan election officials have protections in place to ensure each person receives only one vote and to track every ballot, including the Michigan Qualified Voter File (QVF) which tracks absentee ballot requests, preventing a person from requesting multiple ballots, and voting more than once in an election is illegal in Michigan.
statements.support_span: We have protections in place to ensure election officials track and verify every ballot they send and receive and in every instance we ensure that each person gets only one vote. | once a clerk receives an application from someone whose identity is verified and the signature on the application matches the one on file, it is marked in our Qualified Voter File that that person has requested an absentee ballot... They are not able to request multiples, as this process would flag that they had already requested a ballot any time their information was entered into the QVF. | It is illegal to vote more than once in an election. ... Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel reminded people that it is illegal to vote more than once.

silver.justification: The evidence clarifies that the individual received four ballot applications rather than four actual ballots, noting that these applications were sent by the Center for Voter Information (CVI) specifically to registered voters. Furthermore, election officials and the CVI CEO state that returning multiple applications does not enable multiple votes, as Michigan's Qualified Voter File (QVF) tracks absentee ballot requests to prevent duplicate ballots. State officials emphasize that protections are in place to ensure each person only votes once and that voting more than once is illegal.
